Task: Aluminum Surface Energy
Description: Calculate the surface energy of Aluminum for the given surface by removing periodic boundary conditions in the given direction and computing the energy difference per unit area between the relaxed bulk and the relaxed slab configuration. Use the Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potential and the following simulation parameters. The simulation should replicate the unit cell 5 times in each of the x, y, and z directions. Return the surface energy in electronvolts/Å² units.

Required submission format:
numerical value without units (eg. 56.00)


Available input data:
All the potentials, can be found at /potentials/. Note that in case of reaxff potentials, pair style 'reax/c' has been renamed to 'reaxff' and always use NULL for the control file (cfile), for example, this syntax is correct : pair_style reaxff NULL.

Thought: The structure has been successfully converted to a LAMMPS data file. Now, I need to set up the LAMMPS input script to perform the simulation. This script will include the necessary parameters and commands to calculate the surface energy using the EAM potential. I will write this input script next.
Action: write_file
Action Input: {"path": "/results/2_AUGUST_2025/gpt_4o/react/surface_energy/brief/tasks/aluminum_surface_energy_trial_2/in.aluminum_surface_energy", "content": "
# LAMMPS Input Script for Aluminum Surface Energy Calculation

units metal
atom_style atomic
boundary p p f

read_data aluminum_structure.data

# Define interatomic potential
pair_style eam
pair_coeff * * /potentials/Al99.eam.alloy Al

# Replicate the unit cell
replicate 5 5 5

# Energy minimization
min_style cg
minimize 1e-10 1e-10 100000 100000

# Compute energy
variable bulk_energy equal pe/vol

# Remove periodic boundary in z-direction
change_box all boundary p p s

# Energy minimization for slab
minimize 1e-10 1e-10 100000 100000

# Compute slab energy
variable slab_energy equal pe/vol

# Calculate surface energy
variable surface_energy equal (slab_energy - bulk_energy) / (2*lx*ly)

# Output the surface energy
print "Surface energy = ${surface_energy} eV/Å²"
"}
